_comment: Illustrative spec for a fictional company. Use as a template; replace every value.
source_note: Source: Example Testing Labs IM (Sep-2026); management accounts; AA analysis
fin_note: FY23A-FY26A unaudited management accounts, June year end; FY27F is management forecast.
lead_para: Independent testing, inspection and certification lab for building, product and traffic-enforcement clients across VIC and NSW. Founded 1998; Melbourne HQ; ~95 FTE across three NATA-accredited sites. FY26A revenue $21.0m, adj. EBITDA $2.3m (11.0% margin).
revenue_streams_intro: FY26A $21.0m; 71.1% from two compliance-driven testing divisions.

revenue_streams.name: Acoustics & Vibration
revenue_streams.description: Tests and models noise, vibration and wind on buildings, infrastructure and machinery, required for planning approval; fee-for-service

revenue_streams.name: Safety & Performance
revenue_streams.description: NATA-accredited product testing and certification required before goods can be legally sold; per-test fee

revenue_streams.name: Environmental Monitoring
revenue_streams.description: Installs and runs air-quality and dust monitors on construction sites to meet EPA permit conditions; monthly monitoring fee

revenue_streams.name: Traffic Systems
revenue_streams.description: Tests and calibrates speed and red-light cameras so readings hold up in court; long-term contract with the Victorian Government, its only customer in this division

business_items.label: Revenue model
business_items.text: Fee-for-service and per-test; ~35% from repeat panel work, none contracted beyond the Traffic contract; GP margin 48.0%; no retention data disclosed.

business_items.label: Go-to-market
business_items.text: Wins work via government and tier-1 builder panels; NATA accreditation is the licence to operate; top 10 clients 41.0% of revenue.

business_items.label: Demand driver
business_items.text: Mandatory testing under the NCC and Australian Consumer Law; infrastructure pipeline sustains acoustic work.

chart_notes: Unaudited management accounts; FY26A adj. EBITDA normalised by $0.4m (17.4% of reported)
Revenue CAGR 5.1% flatters: FY26A growth +1.0% as Acoustics volumes softened
GP margin steady at ~48% but adj. EBITDA margin down from 14.4% to 11.0% on overhead growth
Site lease held by vendors' related-party trust, outside the transaction perimeter
FY27F needs +7.6% revenue and margin recovery to 11.9%

transaction.lead: Two founders (50.0% each) seeking a full exit; neither intends to roll equity or stay beyond a 12-month handover. Adj. EBITDA $2.3m sits at the bottom of the $2-10m band. Mandate misfit: 100% exit with no owner-operator rolling equity.
transaction.source: Intermediated: Example Advisory (Melbourne), Jane Citizen; IM received 15-Sep-2026 by APC and RMD; indicative bids due 30-Oct-2026.

recommendation.rationale: Full exit with no rolling founder is outside mandate; declining adj. EBITDA margin and a single-customer Traffic division add risk; compliance-driven demand is the main attraction
gates: Revisit only if a founder will roll at least 20.0% and stay three years
Confirm FY26A normalisations with the advisor

transaction.other_niches: IM flags fire-safety testing and building-envelope consulting. Adjacent AA thematics: NATA-accredited calibration labs, environmental compliance monitoring for construction; no portfolio company overlap.

growing_high_margin.evidence: Revenue CAGR 5.1% FY23A-FY26A, +1.0% in FY26A; adj. EBITDA -17.9% to $2.3m at 11.0%. A 48.0% gross margin does not reach the bottom line.

recurring_revenue.evidence: Fee-for-service and per-test; only the Traffic contract (13.7%) is contracted. Panel repeat work is ~35% but uncommitted.

differentiated.evidence: NATA accreditation and court-grade calibration are hard to replicate. TBC: win rates and pricing power on panel tenders.

large_growing_market.evidence: Testing is mandated under the NCC and Australian Consumer Law, so demand tracks construction and product launches. Market size not quantified in the IM.

fragmented_end_market.evidence: Customers are builders, manufacturers and government; top 10 are 41.0% of revenue, with one government client in Traffic.

supplier_power.commentary: Accredited acoustic engineers are scarce and wage inflation is running ahead of fees. Equipment is commoditised.

buyer_power.commentary: Panel tenders and tier-1 builders squeeze price. Traffic has a single government buyer.

competitive_rivalry.commentary: Competes with national TIC groups and boutique labs. Accreditation limits the field per test type.

threat_of_substitutes.commentary: Testing is legally mandated and must be independent. Some modelling could move in-house at large engineering firms.

threat_of_new_entrants.commentary: NATA accreditation and panel track record take years to build. Well-funded TIC groups could enter by acquisition.
